title: Sub-second consensus with the certifier fix: the epoch-boundary kill re-run
summary: We re-ran the 6 October benchmark (r20261006-0053) on the same fleet shape, ten c3-highcpu-8 validators with Hyperdisk Balanced disks, with the same load generator and the same consensus timing (500 ms maximum header delay, 250 ms minimum header delay, 250 ms maximum batch delay, 5 s vote timeout). The node build changed in one place: a validator that re-proposes an identical header no longer restarts the collection of votes for it. The harness again killed validator-05 59 seconds before an epoch was due to close, this time on the node's own clock, and held it down for 300 seconds. The chain did not stop: the other nine validators kept committing through the outage, the epoch closed on time at 06:37:59 UTC, and chain throughput stayed between 3,085 and 4,355 tx/s in every minute from 06:34 to 06:46. With all ten load generators running, average chain throughput was 3,890 tx/s, against 3,320 tx/s for the run that stalled and 4,177 tx/s for 29 September (r20260929-1647). The median time for a transaction to land was 3.4 s and the 95th percentile 18.0 s (26.1 s on the stalled run, 14.4 s on 29 September). The restarted validator spent 750 seconds in catch-up mode, half the 25 minutes seen on 29 September; it executed blocks at about the rate the loaded chain produced them, so it reached the head only after the load ended. <<RESULT>> one sentence on the tail, once a human decides how to read it: after the main load ended, no block was produced from 06:48:21 to 06:54:33 while two load generators were still sending.

upstream.branch: <<RESULT>> branch name of ba43a1f0e (the certifier fix, fix/certifier-keep-inflight-on-repropose, on top of devnet-bench-10-5-2026 at 964087e02?)
evidence_detail: <<RESULT>> Commit ba43a1f0e is the 6 October benchmark build (964087e02, head of devnet-bench-10-5-2026) plus one change: the certifier keeps its in-flight vote collection when the proposer hands it an identical, re-proposed header, instead of cancelling the outstanding vote requests and starting again. Confirm the parent commit and that nothing else changed.

load.placement: one blaster per validator, in that validator's zone, sending only to it

methodology: Before creating anything, the harness resolved the node image tag adiri:mmap-subsecond-certfix-10-6-2026 to its registry digest and pinned the run to that digest (sha256:caeb6be2…). It ran the pinned image to confirm that it reports telcoin-network 0.1.0 built from commit ba43a1f0e, has the sub-second timestamp fork active from genesis and contains the log messages later checks rely on, and it recorded the committed consensus parameters file and its three delays.
Preflight checked access, tools, quotas and a clean genesis directory, and confirmed the load-generator image built from tn-transaction-generator commit 3644adc, the same image as the 6 October run.

The harness created ten validators and one observer on c3-highcpu-8 (8 vCPU, 16 GB), each with a 100 GB Hyperdisk Balanced boot disk provisioned at 20,000 IOPS and 800 MiB/s, two validators in each of five regions, and opened the consensus ports between the nodes only.
It generated validator keys and built genesis for a separate benchmark chain (chain id 32286, 20-minute epochs).

It finalized each node's configuration with the committed benchmark consensus parameters: maximum header delay 500 ms, minimum header delay 250 ms and maximum batch delay 250 ms, with every other key as in the devnet defaults. The file sets no vote timeout, so the node's built-in 5 s applied. It then started the chain.
It relabelled each node's metrics agent so that every sample from these nodes is recorded under the benchmark network, never the live devnet.

It restarted the nodes one at a time with RPC open on the internal network, waiting after each until the node answered with the benchmark chain id and consensus rounds were advancing. Each node's boot lines had to show the pinned commit, the three consensus delays, the 5,000 ms vote timeout and the fork schedule recorded at the gate, and all eleven did. An on-node sampler was then started on each node.

A health gate confirmed that all eleven nodes reported to Prometheus under the benchmark network with consensus rounds rising, and a read of the ConsensusRegistry through an RPC tunnel confirmed the 1,200 s epoch duration.
It deployed the devnet contract set that the mixed workload calls.

The first two attempts to start the load (blast indexes 0 and 1) stopped before any load was sent, because e2-standard-2 machines were out of stock in australia-southeast1-c and the two load generators for that zone could not be created; the harness deleted the generators it had created and kept their records apart. The third attempt (blast index 2), the one published here, used n2-standard-2 (2 vCPU, 8 GB) for the funder and all ten load generators. Each attempt re-ran the funder.

A one-off funder VM funded 600 sender accounts for each of ten load generators, one per validator in that validator's zone and sending only to it, and the generators then started together at 06:05:38 UTC.
Each generator ran 120 s of warm-up, 2,400 s of mixed load across 13 transaction types and up to 180 s of cool-down, cut short after 30 s in which none of the generator's own transactions landed.

The chaos schedule was timed to the chain's epochs. Before the load generators were created, the harness read the ConsensusRegistry at a pinned block to locate the epoch boundaries and chose the first epoch close at least 600 s into the planned mixed phase, 06:37:57 UTC. It set validator-05's container to be killed with SIGKILL 59 s before that close and held down, the node to be restarted 300 s after the kill, and the observer's node to be restarted 300 s after that. Each action was staged on the target node and fired by the node's own clock: the kill began at 06:36:58.139, the restart at 06:41:58.179 and the observer restart at 06:46:58.067, each less than 0.2 s after its planned second. Epoch 4 opened at 06:37:59, so the outage crossed the boundary. The run had one blast and no injected network delay.
During the run the harness sampled the fleet's highest block and recorded any period in which it did not advance between samples as a commit stall.

Afterwards the harness collected each generator's results and the on-node sampler files, merged the generator results with aggregate.py, derived the sizing figures with derive-sizing.py, and pulled 60-second machine metrics from Cloud Monitoring and 15-second node metrics from Prometheus. <<RESULT>> confirm for this run: before teardown deleted anything, the run's results were copied to a persistent storage bucket.

Teardown began at 07:13 UTC. It saved every node's logs, sampler files and service journal, then deleted the fleet, which was gone by <<RESULT>> UTC. The publishing pipeline then read each node's logged commit, consensus delays, vote timeout and fork schedule back from those logs.
caveats: The chain did not stall this time. Validator-05 was killed 59 s before the epoch close, as planned, and the other nine validators kept committing: chain throughput in the one-minute buckets from 06:34 to 06:46 UTC ranged from 3,085 to 4,355 tx/s, the longest run of seconds without a landed transaction was 9 s (from 06:38:00, at the epoch boundary), and epoch 4 opened on time at 06:37:59. In the all-generators window the average was 3,921 tx/s before the kill and 3,833 tx/s after it. On the 6 October run (r20261006-0053) the same kill, 42 s before the close, was followed by 301 s with no landed transaction.

Validator-05 restarted at 06:41:58 UTC and was in catch-up mode from the first Prometheus sample at 06:42:25 to 06:54:55 (750 s). Its sampler shows its executed block held at 27,969 until about 06:44:30, then rising by about 800 to 870 blocks a minute, close to the 780 a minute the loaded chain produced, so the gap of about 5,700 blocks stayed level while the load ran. It reached the chain head, block 36,577, at 06:54:31, after block production had stopped at 06:48:21. Load generator 05, which sends only to validator-05, landed no transactions from 06:38 to the end of its mixed phase at 06:47:48; the 8,294 transactions it sent after the restart waited in validator-05's pool until the validator rejoined. On 29 September the same node spent 1,500 s in catch-up mode; on the 6 October run the chain was stalled through the outage, so there was almost nothing to catch up on.

Eight load generators finished their setup transactions within 12 s and began their mixed phase between 06:07:48 and 06:07:52 UTC. Generator 04 took 161 s and began at 06:10:21. Generator 03 stopped waiting at the 600-second preamble limit with 62 of its 600 senders still missing a setup step (134 setup transactions unlanded) and began at 06:17:40. Both are the australia-southeast1 generators. The all-generators window is therefore 06:17:40 to 06:47:48 UTC (1,808 s), and the merged mixed window, 06:07:48 to 06:57:40 UTC (2,992 s, average 3,305 tx/s), ends with about ten minutes in which only generators 03 and 04, then only 03, were running. On the 6 October run eight generators hit the preamble limit and only two started on time.

<<RESULT>> (decide the wording; facts follow) After the eight on-time generators stopped at 06:47:48 to 06:47:52 UTC, no block was produced from 06:48:21 (block 36,577) to 06:54:33 (block 36,578, no transactions), although consensus rounds kept advancing on all ten validators at about 158 a minute and sub-DAGs were committed at about 1.3 a second, and generators 03 (mixed phase until 06:57:40) and 04 (until 06:50:21) were still sending. Validator-03 kept sealing batches in that period. About 15,800 transactions landed in the minute from 06:54, as validator-05 rejoined, and none after that before the empty block that closed epoch 4 at 06:57:59. Generators 03, 04 and 05 ended with 9,888, 9,788 and 9,827 accepted transactions that never landed. The harness recorded 06:48:31 to 06:52:04 as a commit stall (its watch ended while the height was still flat). Consensus did not stall, but transactions sent to validators 03 and 04 stopped landing; the cause is not established.

The offered load was uneven. Generators 03 and 04 sent about 239,000 and 401,000 transactions over the blast, against about 820,000 to 1.9 million for the other eight. Their transactions also waited longest: median time to land 14.6 s for generator 03 and 6.8 s for generator 04 (95th percentile 378.5 s and 325.7 s), against 7 to 26 s at the 95th percentile for the other generators except 07 (303.5 s). These waits are part of the whole-blast p95 of 18.0 s.

Every generator's 99th-percentile time to land is between 301 s and 635 s. Each generator logged that its validator had dropped transactions it had already accepted, about 23,600 times across the ten generators (about 23,700 on the 6 October run), and resent them; those transactions make up most of the slow tail.

Consensus committed less often under load than on the 6 October run: about 0.42 sub-DAGs and 0.90 rounds a second before the kill, against 0.59 and 1.21, and 0.32 and 0.69 while validator-05 was down. The commit latency p95 rose from 4.77 to 4.88 s to 5.75 to 6.25 s. The cause has not been looked at.

The load generators ran on n2-standard-2, not the e2-standard-2 used on 6 October and 29 September, because e2 capacity was out of stock in australia-southeast1-c. Both are 2-vCPU machines, but the load-generator machine type differs between this run and both comparison runs.

Against the 6 October run the node build differs by the certifier change and the load-generator machine type differs; the generator image, fleet shape, consensus timing and chaos plan are the same. The 6 October run stalled for 301 s inside its all-generators window and this one did not, so the difference in averages mostly reflects the stall. The comparison with 29 September (r20260929-1647) also spans a different node build and the 3 s, 1 s, 1 s devnet consensus timing, so no difference can be assigned to any one change.
<<RESULT>> The harness working tree had uncommitted changes when the run was deployed (harness 3a31603, dirty). Say what they were, or that they did not touch the deploy or measurement path.
This configuration has been run once, so run-to-run variation is not measured.
The tag adiri:mmap-subsecond-certfix-10-6-2026 is mutable. The harness resolved it to digest sha256:caeb6be2… before any node was created, and every node ran that digest.
